_note: US11R scenario questions: Sam's first working set (6 items), BK-ruled 2026-09-21. Order is load-bearing - a saved town remembers its place in this list by position - so append only. Prompts, options, answers and hints are Sam's verbatim; *asterisks* in a line mark his emphasis and render as italics. The two written items' exemplars and checklists are the build session's, marked on each item.

on_resolve._note: What resolving a question gives the town: a small drop in unrest, less for every hint used (the costed-hint model, as an in-fiction cost since the build has no equilibrium score), and one bounded bend - a town that understands how it is governed pays its taxes a little less grudgingly. Engineering defaults chosen by the build session 2026-09-21, not content and not a balance pass.

items.prompt: Your sheriff arrested a man and held him for a week without ever charging him with a crime. A councilman objects. What's he objecting to?

options.label: A failure of Rule of Law

hints: Rule of Law is about whether the law gets enforced at all. This isn't about whether a law existed.
This is about whether the *process* the law promises — charges, a hearing — actually happened.
The man wasn't let off the hook. He was denied the steps the law says he's owed first.
items._source: Sam, from-sam-2026-09-21-scenario-question-content-and-third-archetype.md section 2, BK-ruled 2026-09-21 - prompt, options, answer and hints verbatim (item 1)

items.prompt: Your town wants to set its own tax rate, but a regional authority says it needs their approval first. What principle is at stake?
hints: This is about who holds power — one level of government, or several sharing it.
Federalism is the word for power split between a central authority and local ones.
Your town is the "local" half of that split.
items._source: Sam, from-sam-2026-09-21-scenario-question-content-and-third-archetype.md section 2, BK-ruled 2026-09-21 - prompt, options, answer and hints verbatim (item 2)
items._hint_names_answer: Hint 2 names the correct option outright ('Federalism is the word for...'). Wired verbatim because BK ruled the item as written; flagged to Sam in the 2026-09-21 build handoff. test/nb/questions.test.js allows this one item by id and no other.

items.prompt: Your council wants to spend the treasury on a new road. The mayor can veto it. What keeps that veto itself from becoming absolute power?

options.label: Nothing — the mayor's word is final

hints: Look for the word that means one power checking another, which is checked right back.
If the veto had no answer, that's not checks and balances — that's just one office holding all the power.
Somebody else in the system needs their own move in response to the veto.
items._source: Sam, from-sam-2026-09-21-scenario-question-content-and-third-archetype.md section 2, BK-ruled 2026-09-21 - prompt, options, answer and hints verbatim (item 3)

items.prompt: Write one sentence that sets the scene for why your town's unrest is rising — what was already true before this crisis hit?
hints: Don't describe the crisis itself yet — what was already going on before it?
Think tax rate, policing level, or a decision you made turns ago — the conditions, not the event.
One clause with "already" or "for years" in it usually does the job.
items.exemplar: For years before this, the town had been taxed close to its limit while the watch stayed thin, so people were already stretched and already uneasy when the trouble came.
checklist: It describes a condition, not the crisis itself.
It names something that was already true — a tax rate, the policing, or a decision made earlier.
It shows that condition came first, with words like "already" or "for years."

items.prompt: A widow in your town can't sign the deed to her own house without a male relative co-signing. What's the legal principle that allows this?
hints: This isn't about a right being denied for a crime — it's about a right never granted in the first place.
It's specifically about a married or widowed woman's legal identity being absorbed into a man's.
You read the actual term for this in your Casefile B documents.
items._source: Sam, from-sam-2026-09-21-scenario-question-content-and-third-archetype.md section 2, BK-ruled 2026-09-21 - prompt, options, answer and hints verbatim (item 5)

items.prompt: Your advisor reports: 'Unemployment is climbing.' Add ONE sentence that explains why that matters for your town right now.
hints: Don't repeat the fact — say what it *causes* or *risks*.
Think about what unemployment does to unrest, tax revenue, or who's available to work.
A sentence starting "This means..." or "As a result..." usually gets you there.
items.exemplar: This means fewer people are earning wages the town can tax, so the treasury shrinks at the same moment more people are angry about how hard work is to find.
checklist: It says what the fact causes or risks, instead of repeating it.
It ties that effect to something in your town — unrest, tax money, or who is available to work.
It uses a cause-and-effect connector, like "This means" or "As a result."
